title: Grateful Dead Live at Denver Coliseum on 1973-11-21

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a high‑energy ’73 show highlighted by the legendary Playin’ > El Paso > Playin’ > Wharf Rat > Playin’ > Morning Dew jam sandwich.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its soaring energy, tight transitions and an all‑time great jam sandwich that threads Playin' through El Paso, Wharf Rat and Morning Dew. Reviewers note a clean, crisp soundboard recording with only minor pitch‑shift quirks and occasional splices, making the show both musically and technically enjoyable.

ai_rating.rationale: 22 reviews overwhelmingly 4–5 stars (average ≈ 4.7); most comment on superb playing and clear sound, with only minor technical complaints.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear, crisp mix; occasional half‑step pitch raise, a few level adjustments and splices noted; overall very clean with good instrument separation. Minor tuning slips mentioned but do not detract from listenability.

standout_songs: Playin' In The Band > El Paso > Playin' > Wharf Rat > Playin' > Morning Dew
show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong first set with tight segues (Jack Straw, Here Comes Sunshine, Brokedown Palace) leading into the epic second‑set jam sandwich; Weather Report Suite and Truckin' close the show smoothly.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead is often described as forward in the mix, exploratory, inventive (especially on Jack Straw and the jam sandwich), though a few reviewers note missed notes/tuning slips.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh delivers solid bass lines with occasional “fuzzy‑fat” tones; some mention missed notes but overall praised for supporting the jam dynamics.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm work and vocal harmonies highlighted on Big River and Jack Straw; noted for near‑solo moments and strong presence in the mix.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboard work gets kudos for a great break in Big River and overall contribution to the jam textures.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming praised for its snap on Big River and tight feel throughout the extended jams.
